ov: Segmented worms related to earthworms, with a sucker at each end. Of about 680 species, most live in fresh water, some on land and about 100 in the sea. The best known feed on blood, but others are predators of small invertebrates. They live everywhere except Antarctica.
rg: Worldwide except Antarctica, most abundant in temperate northern lakes and ponds.
df: Blood of vertebrates for many species; others hunt small invertebrates.
fx: A medicinal leech can drink up to ten times its body weight in one meal, then go a year without feeding.
The US Food and Drug Administration classed leech therapy as a medical device in 2004.
